chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Cricket Smith, soloist of the new band
summary: Briggs describes Cricket Smith, who stayed in New York when Europe's band left, as a good player with a fine tone and a wonderful person.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You see. And we all made, what you call today auditions. That is when the band, the St. Marks Brass Band played and he would come and listen to us, and choose, and -I happened to be one that was selected to be in this orchestra, this band. And the soloist of this new band was Cricket Smith. You heard of him?
Oh yes, sure.
He was a personal friend. I owe him quite a lot.
Well, Cricket Smith didn't go over with the James Reese Europe?
No, he didn't, no.
He was here?
Yes. He stayed in New York. But he was not drafted, you see; it was a question of the draft.
I see, yes.
Briggs
He was not drafted, they were not all drafted, you see. If they were all drafted, nothing left. (Laughter).
Right.
So, Cricket, and so was Lieutenant Fred Simpson, he was also at the Ziegfeld Follies, you see.
Right.
And Cricket stayed. He was also with Jim Europe's band at first, but he was not drafted to go over.
So, he didn't go.
No, no, he stayed. And he became first and soloist with this new outfit.
I see. What kind of a player was he, Cricket Smith?
Good. Yes, good.
Big registered tone?
